prompts.title: Motion without a push
prompts.seed: Student A says, "If the puck is still moving, something must keep pushing it." Student B says, "No, because acceleration and velocity are different."
prompts.question: Discuss what would happen on an ideal frictionless surface and on a rough floor. Each student must use the phrase "net force" correctly.
prompts.facilitator_move: Ask Student A to propose a test distinguishing constant velocity from acceleration. Invite Student B to challenge with a rough-floor counterexample. Avoid stating the complete answer first.

prompts.title: Truck and car disagreement
prompts.seed: Student A says, "The truck exerts more force because it is heavier." Student B says, "The forces are equal but accelerations can differ."
prompts.question: Label the two interacting bodies and identify the forces for each. Explain which mass matters for acceleration.
prompts.facilitator_move: Ask each student to name the source and recipient of one force before accepting a conclusion.

prompts.title: The static-friction trap
prompts.seed: Student A says, "There is no friction because the box does not move." Student B says, "The friction always equals mu_s times the normal force."
prompts.question: A 12 N horizontal push does not move the box. Use Newton's second law to decide the actual friction force and explain why both statements can be wrong.
prompts.facilitator_move: Request a horizontal free-body diagram and ask for net force before asking about maximum static friction.
